title: Findings from Keppel Offshore & Marine Corruption Probe
what_it_is: Findings from Keppel Offshore & Marine Corruption Probe

sections.label: Keppel bribery prosecution questions
sections.summary: Questions ask the Prime Minister about difficulties in charging Keppel Offshore & Marine officers and about reassuring the public the decision not to prosecute six former staff is not cronyism.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: asked the Prime Minister what specific difficulties were faced by the Attorney-General's Chambers and Corrupt Practices Investigation Bureau in considering whether to prefer charges against the officers of Keppel Offshore & Marine Limited (KOM) over corrupt payments from KOM to Petrobas and Sete Brasil in Brazil from 2001 to 2014, despite KOM's admissions under both the Deferred Prosecution Agreement with the US Department of Justice and the Brazilian leniency agreement.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
sentences.text: asked the Prime Minister what information or evidence can be given to reassure the public that the decision not to prosecute the six former staff of Keppel Offshore & Marine Limited involved in the S$73 million bribe payments case has nothing to do with their connections and that this is not an example of cronyism.

sections.label: Keppel bribery warnings concerns
sections.summary: Questions ask whether higher KOM officials knew of the bribery scheme and about concerns the stern warnings to six former employees are too light.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: asked the Prime Minister whether the Corrupt Practices Investigation Bureau's investigations into the bribery scheme by Keppel Offshore & Marine Limited (KOM) to obtain contracts from Petrobas and Sete Brasil in Brazil from 2001 to 2014 show that, apart from the six persons issued warnings by the Bureau, there were officials higher up the hierarchy of KOM who were aware of, or were wilfully ignorant of, the bribery scheme before or during its lifespan.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
sentences.text: asked the Prime Minister regarding the recent case where the CPIB issued stern warnings to six former employees of Keppel Offshore & Marine Limited for bribery offences (a) what is the Government’s response to concerns that the penalty is too light, as some offenders have been jailed for much smaller sums of money; and (b) in view of the multinational nature of the alleged transactions, what measures can be taken to improve the deterrence and prosecution of such cross-boundary corruption.

sections.label: Zero tolerance and CPIB powers
sections.summary: Questions ask whether zero tolerance on corruption remains, CPIB's policy on foreign bribery cases, and amending the Prevention of Corruption Act 1960.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
sentences.text: asked the Prime Minister (a) whether zero tolerance on corruption remains to be the Government’s position; and (b) if so, whether the decision to issue stern warnings to the six individuals who were formerly senior management staff of Keppel Offshore & Marine Limited involved in the bribery case undermines that position and signals a lack of political will to stamp out corruption.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: asked the Prime Minister what is CPIB’s policy in determining the circumstances in which it will investigate foreign bribery cases involving Singapore citizens as provided for in section 37 of the Prevention of Corruption Act 1960.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
sentences.text: asked the Prime Minister in light of the conditional warning in lieu of prosecution against six former senior management staff of Keppel Offshore & Marine Limited over bribe payments, whether the Government will consider amending the Prevention of Corruption Act 1960 to expand the powers of the CPIB to facilitate investigations outside of jurisdiction and the available penalties to include compounding offences with profit disgorgement or restitution for appropriate cases.

sections.label: Categories of Members' questions
sections.summary: The questions raised by Members fall into eight broad categories, including why stern warnings were issued and sufficiency of the Prevention of Corruption Act.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The questions raised by Members fall into the following broad categories: (a) why were the six individuals issued with stern warnings instead of being prosecuted; (b) whether, and if so why, the Deferred Prosecution Agreement (DPA) and the accompanying Statement of Facts (SOF) are insufficient to mount a prosecution; (c) details of the investigations or decision to issue stern warnings; (d) why the six individuals in question were not named and whether they should be; (e) statistics on stern warnings and prosecutions; (f) whether the decision to issue stern warnings, instead of prosecuting, will affect our zero tolerance stance on corruption and reputation; (g) corruption in foreign jurisdictions; and (h) sufficiency of the Prevention of Corruption Act (PCA).

sections.label: Lack of sufficient evidence
sections.summary: There is a lack of sufficient documentary or witness evidence to establish any criminal charge beyond reasonable doubt against a specific individual, and AGC made mutual legal assistance requests over five years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Simply put – there is a lack of sufficient evidence either documentary or through witnesses, which would establish any criminal charge beyond a reasonable doubt against a specific individual.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The Attorney-General's Chambers (AGC) has made a number of mutual legal assistance requests over five years.

sections.label: Insufficient evidence against six individuals
sections.summary: The agencies do not have sufficient evidence to show beyond reasonable doubt that any of the six individuals were guilty of an offence.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: In short, the agencies do not have sufficient evidence that would show, beyond reasonable doubt that any of the six individuals were guilty of an offence.

sections.label: MLA requests confidential outcome
sections.summary: MLA requests are confidential and either yielded no usable evidence or were unhelpful to the case.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The contents and outcome of these MLA requests are confidential, but I can inform the House that they have either not yielded evidence that could be used to secure a conviction before our Courts, or the responses have not been helpful in advancing the case.

sections.label: CPIB investigation evidential difficulties
sections.summary: CPIB investigated thoroughly but cross-border nature and absent key witnesses left evidential difficulties preventing prosecution in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: CPIB has conducted as thorough an investigation as it could with the information and powers that it possessed.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: However, given the cross-border nature of this case and absence of key witnesses, CPIB's investigations could not overcome the evidential difficulties for the purposes of prosecution in a Singapore Court.

sections.label: Zero tolerance policy unchanged
sections.summary: From 2017 to 2021 CPIB issued an average of 138 warnings annually and prosecuted 139 individuals, with no change to zero tolerance policy.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: From 2017 to 2021, CPIB has issued an average of 138 warnings annually and 139 individuals were prosecuted.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Questions have been asked on the impact of Singapore's zero tolerance policy on corruption and reputation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: There is no change in Singapore's zero tolerance policy on corruption.

sections.label: Foreign evidence needs international cooperation
sections.summary: When evidence is outside Singapore, agencies depend on international cooperation, and Parliament cannot empower CPIB abroad due to territorial sovereignty.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Hence, when evidence resides outside Singapore, our agencies are dependent on international cooperation and foreign authorities to facilitate their investigations and secure the relevant evidence.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: This Parliament cannot legislate to empower CPIB to conduct investigations in foreign jurisdictions because that would run afoul of territorial sovereignty.

sections.label: PP warnings and re-evaluation
sections.summary: CPIB and AGC reviewed documents and the PP found them insufficient, but will re-evaluate if new compelling evidence arises.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: CPIB and AGC have undertaken a careful and thorough review of the documents, including the DPAs and plea bargains and the PP has advised that those are insufficient to meet the burden of proof.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: But if subsequently new and compelling evidence comes up, the PP can and will re-evaluate the decision.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The PP's decision to issue stern warnings should be understood in that context.

sections.label: MLA request short outcome
sections.summary: The MLA request outcome is that responses either yielded no conviction evidence or were unhelpful to advancing the case.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: How would you know what that person would say?

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: So, the short outcome of the request for mutual legal assistance is, as I explained in my earlier answer, that they either have not yielded evidence that could be used to secure conviction before the Courts or the responses have not been helpful in advancing the case.

sections.label: CPIB investigation and constructive knowledge
sections.summary: CPIB investigates offences under the Prevention of Corruption Act, but there is insufficient evidence to mount a prosecution.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: But coming back to Mr Singh's question, that is why I asked him whether he is suggesting that constructive knowledge is an offence.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Therefore, if the question is whether the investigation included determining if there was constructive knowledge, the answer is: if constructive knowledge is not an offence then there is no reason for CPIB to be investigating this.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: CPIB investigates offences under the Prevention of Corruption Act and that is what they have done.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: And in this case, unfortunately, there is insufficient evidence for them to mount a prosecution.

sections.label: Minister's reply on MLA requests
sections.summary: The speaker says the Minister did not reply to his second supplementary question on MLAs, though she earlier mentioned three MLA requests to Brazil.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: On the second supplementary question I asked with regard to MLAs, I do not believe that Minister has replied, although in her early response, she did say three MLA requests were put to Brazil, if I understand.

sections.label: MLA requests sent to Brazil
sections.summary: AGC sent three MLA requests to Brazil, and AGC and CPIB sent another MLA request to interview potential material witnesses.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Earlier on in my answer, I had said that AGC has sent three mutual legal assistance (MLA) requests to Brazil to secure evidence that was needed.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: And AGC and CPIB also sent an MLA request to another relevant foreign authority to interview other potential material witnesses.

sections.label: Key material witnesses unavailable
sections.summary: The problem is that key material witnesses are not available.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The problem is that key material witnesses are not available.

sections.label: AGC threshold for filing charges
sections.summary: Filing charges with insufficient basis does not make a strong justice system, and AGC cannot get over that threshold in this case.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Otherwise, if you just go around filing charges with insufficient basis, that will not make for a strong justice system.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: And that is the threshold that AGC feels that it is not able to get over, in this particular case.

sections.label: No admissions from six persons
sections.summary: CPIB has no admissions or confessions from the six persons, and one foreign witness is unwilling to give evidence in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: In response to Ms Sylvia Lim's first question as to whether CPIB has been able to obtain admissions or confessions for those six persons, my understanding is that CPIB has not had any admissions or confessions from the six persons.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The second one, when she asked about the foreign witness, I will refer back to my earlier answer where I actually said two things.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: I said there is one foreign witness who gave evidence in other proceedings which could have been relevant to establishing offences in Singapore, but that foreign witness is not willing to voluntarily give evidence in Singapore.

sections.label: Differences in US and CPIB accounts
sections.summary: The speaker says there are differences between what was said in the US and what was told to CPIB in this case.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: What I do know, and I am able to say based on what has been informed to me, is that in this particular case, what was said in the US and what has been told to CPIB, there are differences.

sections.label: Bribery awareness and investigation
sections.summary: The speaker says that if authorities learn of bribery or an offence, it will be investigated.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Has the Government ever been aware of Singaporeans paying bribes to foreign officials but decided not to take them to task on the basis that bribery is sometimes seen as necessary to win contracts in countries where corruption is rife and that winning these contracts benefit Singaporean companies and Singaporean employees?

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: I think I can say this much in response to that question – which is that if it comes to the attention of our authorities that an act of bribery or an offence has occurred, it will be investigated.

sections.label: Stern warning meaning
sections.summary: A stern warning is given when you feel you cannot give a complete clean bill of health.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The answer to that is, a stern warning is given when you feel that you cannot say that you give a complete clean bill of health.

sections.label: Stern warning as middle device
sections.summary: The stern warning device is described as the something in between.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The stern warning device is the something in between.

sections.label: Keppel DPA compliance conditions
sections.summary: Under the DPA, Keppel had to implement compliance and ethics programmes, review internal accounting controls, and modify its compliance programme.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Under the DPA, one of the requirements or the conditions for the Deferred Prosecution, was that Keppel would have to continue to implement compliance and ethics programmes designed to prevent and detect violations of the FCPA and other anti-corruption laws.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: And they also undertook to review their internal accounting controls, policies and procedures regarding compliance with the FCPA and other applicable anti-corruption laws.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: They also agreed to modify their compliance programme, including internal controls, compliance policies and procedures.
